### Los Angeles Recurring Board Game Communities & Venues Shortlist

Below is a verified shortlist of 14 recurring board game groups, store venues, library programs, and dedicated event nights across Greater Los Angeles, drawn from 4 distinct source types: **Meetup**, **Venue/Store websites & calendars**, **Eventbrite**, and **Public Library community calendars (LAPL)**.

---

### Part 1: The 14 Recurring Groups & Venues

#### 1. Board Game and Brew Meetup
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.meetup.com/west-la-settlers-of-catan-meetup/
* **Source Type:** Meetup
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Santa Monica / Westside (hosted at Santa Monica Brew Works, 1920 Colorado Ave C, Santa Monica, CA 90404)
* **Play Focus:** Catan and expansions, social deduction games (Secret Hitler, Blood on the Clocktower, Avalon, One Night Ultimate Werewolf), light-to-mid strategy, party games (Magic Maze, Exploding Kittens), and member-brought games.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Very beginner-friendly and social; welcoming to people who haven't played modern board games before.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Free meetup attendance; purchasing drinks (beer or non-alcoholic) or food from the brewery/food trucks is customary to support the host venue.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** 5 upcoming events scheduled, meeting weekly on Saturdays or Sundays (1,670+ members).

#### 2. LA Game Crew – "The Grotto" @ Odyssey Games
* **Group / Event Page:** https://lagamecrew.com (Venue: Odyssey Games, 1795 E Colorado Blvd, Pasadena, CA 91106)
* **Source Type:** Community Website & Store Venue
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Pasadena / San Gabriel Valley (SGV)
* **Play Focus:** Dual-track all-day gaming sessions: 2:00 PM – 7:00 PM focuses on heavy strategy and Euro games (often 3+ hours long), followed by 7:00 PM – 11:00 PM welcoming newcomers with shorter, social, and accessible gateway games.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Dual-tier (Hardcore strategy in the afternoon; Beginner-friendly in the evening).
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** $5 per person all-day access pass (paid at venue); outside food is permitted.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Active 2026 event schedule published on their website with quarterly marathons (May, August, November 2026) and linked Meetup/WhatsApp communities.

#### 3. Geeky Teas & Games Open Play & Community Hub
* **Group / Event Page:** https://visitburbank.com/what-to-do/shopping/geeky-teas/ (Venue site: https://www.geekyteasandgames.com/ at 900 W Alameda Ave, Burbank, CA 91506)
* **Source Type:** Board Game Shop / Cafe / Community Calendar
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Burbank / The Valley
* **Play Focus:** Open tabletop gaming from an enormous in-house board game library (hundreds of titles ranging from gateway games like Ticket to Ride and Carcassonne to mid-weight Euros, wargaming, and RPGs).
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Welcoming to all skill levels; staff can recommend and orient players, while private tables allow for deeper campaigns.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** $5 day pass grants all-day access to the game library and tables; teas and snacks available for purchase.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Actively operating in 2026 with daily open table hours, community Discord, and regular hosted events (such as First Play LA playtesting).

#### 4. Board Game Night @ GAME CULT LA
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.eventbrite.com/e/board-game-night-game-cult-la-tickets-1979630653575
* **Source Type:** Eventbrite
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Downtown Los Angeles (Studio Cult, 1339 S Hill St, Los Angeles, CA 90015 – Central LA / South Park)
* **Play Focus:** 100+ curated modern board games, party games, and social deduction. Frequently played games include Blood on the Clocktower, Betrayal at House on the Hill, Wavelength, Secret Hitler, 7 Wonders, Wingspan, Codenames, Azul, and Dominion.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Very beginner-friendly social mixer vibe with a unique arts/studio aesthetic; ages 21+.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** $17.85 admission ticket through Eventbrite; beer, seltzers, and drinks available for purchase.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Over 100 past events hosted, meeting every Tuesday night with dates scheduled throughout 2026.

#### 5. Friday Night Board Gaming @ Paper Hero's Games
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.meetup.com/fridaynightboardgaming/
* **Source Type:** Meetup / Game Store Community
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Sherman Oaks / The Valley (Paper Hero's Games, 14109 Burbank Blvd, Sherman Oaks, CA 91401)
* **Play Focus:** Gateway Euros (Catan, Ticket to Ride) up through mid-weight and heavy strategy Euros (Suburbia, Power Grid, Terraforming Mars, Railways of the World), as well as wargames and card games.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Accommodates beginners (regulars will teach rules), but leans comfortably into authentic hobby/strategy board gaming.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Free drop-in / no required fee shown (store merchandise purchase appreciated).
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Meets every Friday late afternoon/evening; 1,890 members; active core of 10–20 weekly regulars.

#### 6. East Valley Board Games
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.meetup.com/east-valley-board-games/
* **Source Type:** Meetup
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Sherman Oaks / The Valley (hosted Sunday afternoons at Paper Hero's Games, 14109 Burbank Blvd)
* **Play Focus:** Modern board games, light-to-mid strategy, party games, and word games: Terraforming Mars, Pandemic, Azul, Sushi Go!, Catan, King of Tokyo, Taboo, Dixit, and Ticket to Ride.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Beginner to intermediate friendly; focused on friendly, cooperative, and sporting interaction among adults 21+.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Free RSVP / no fee shown.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Active calendar with sessions scheduled into autumn 2026 (e.g. Sep 27, Oct 11, Oct 25, 2026); 1,420+ members.

#### 7. Long Beach Board Gamers
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.meetup.com/long-beach-fun-times-meetup-group/
* **Source Type:** Meetup
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Long Beach / South Bay & Harbor Area (hosted at The Wicked Wolf, 2332 Pacific Ave, Long Beach, CA 90806)
* **Play Focus:** Diverse mix of modern casual and hobby board games across multiple tables; players bring, pitch, and teach their favorite games.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Beginner-friendly, non-competitive, social atmosphere (21+).
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Free admission; requires purchase of at least 1 beverage from the venue (cocktails, beer, mocktails, or non-alcoholic options).
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** 11 upcoming events scheduled on Meetup; meets every Wednesday evening at 6:00 PM; 1,990+ members; active community Discord.

#### 8. Studious Game Night (Chinatown LA Community Events)
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.meetup.com/chinatown-la/events/316426922/
* **Source Type:** Meetup
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Chinatown / Downtown Los Angeles (Studious Coworking Space, 418 Bamboo Ln A, Los Angeles, CA 90012 – Central LA / Eastside adjacent)
* **Play Focus:** Accessible modern board games, casual social games, potluck snacks, and a parallel arts & crafts table.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Highly beginner-friendly and low-pressure community social night.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** $10 admission at the door (or via advance Venmo) to cover the coworking space rental.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Active event with 33 RSVPs for Friday, Sep 18, 2026; 630+ reviews on Chinatown LA Community Events.

#### 9. First Play: L.A. Board Game Playtesters
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.meetup.com/first-play-los-angeles-board-game-playtesters/
* **Source Type:** Meetup / Game Designer Community
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Burbank / The Valley (Geeky Teas & Games, 900 W Alameda Ave, Burbank, CA 91506)
* **Play Focus:** Playtesting unpublished board game prototypes, rulebook clarity testing, and design feedback, combined with open play and a community board game swap/free store.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Unique creative niche; open to anyone willing to learn unreleased games and offer constructive feedback.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** $8 day pass paid to Geeky Teas at the front desk for all-day store play.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Scheduled monthly event with 27 RSVPs; 1,960+ members.

#### 10. Modern Table Games @ LAPL Venice Branch Library
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.lapl.org/events/modern-table-games-0 (Branch: https://www.lapl.org/branches/venice)
* **Source Type:** Public Library Calendar (Los Angeles Public Library)
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Venice / Westside (501 S. Venice Blvd, Venice, CA 90291)
* **Play Focus:** Gateway hobby board games (Settlers of Catan, Ticket to Ride, Splendor) alongside classic favorites (Monopoly, Scrabble); players may bring their own games.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Very beginner-friendly; volunteer library hosts are on hand specifically to teach rules to newcomers (ages 16+).
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Free (no fees; games and supplies supported by Friends of Venice Library).
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Recurring monthly Saturday afternoon listing on LAPL branch calendar.

#### 11. Board Game Café @ LAPL Baldwin Hills Branch Library
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.lapl.org/events/board-game-cafe
* **Source Type:** Public Library Calendar (Los Angeles Public Library)
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Baldwin Hills / Crenshaw (2906 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90016 – Central / South LA)
* **Play Focus:** Relaxed adult board gaming, open play using library-supplied titles or member-brought games.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Beginner-friendly community drop-in.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Free.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Scheduled and held on LAPL calendar in September 2026.

#### 12. Guildhall (Burbank)
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.guildhall.tv (About: https://www.guildhall.tv/about)
* **Source Type:** Venue Website / Gastropub
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Burbank / The Valley (300 S Victory Blvd, Burbank, CA 91502; secondary location in Whittier)
* **Play Focus:** Dedicated "nerd bar" and gastropub featuring a library of 200+ free-to-play board games, ranging from quick party titles to Euro strategy, alongside craft drinks and esports streaming.
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Beginner-friendly, casual drop-in social environment.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Free board game play; food and drink purchase customary as a dining establishment.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Fully operating restaurant/bar in 2026 with open 7-day-a-week operating hours.

#### 13. Westside Tabletop Adventure Games
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.meetup.com/westside-tabletop-adventure-games/
* **Source Type:** Meetup
* **Neighborhood / Area:** West Los Angeles / Westside
* **Play Focus:** Indie board games from small publishers, DIY wargames, and Old-School Renaissance (OSR) adventure tabletop RPGs (Shadowdark, Cairn, Mork Borg, Classic D&D).
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Leans hobbyist / enthusiast, but welcomes curious players interested in non-mainstream, rules-light adventure systems.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Free meetup membership; venue costs vary by specific event location.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** 540+ members with active community discussions.

#### 14. Next-Gen Games Community & Open Play
* **Group / Event Page:** https://www.nextgengames.la/service/calendar/
* **Source Type:** Game Store Calendar
* **Neighborhood / Area:** Mid-City / Pico-Robertson (5450 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90019 – Central LA / Westside border)
* **Play Focus:** Friendly local game store featuring open tabletop gaming tables, miniature wargames, board games, and trading card games (MTG, Pokémon).
* **Beginner vs. Hardcore:** Mixed crowd; casual drop-ins welcome alongside organized leagues.
* **Cost / Purchase Requirement:** Open table play is generally free or nominal store purchase; organized tournaments have specific entry fees.
* **Visible Evidence of Being Active:** Active WPN Premium store operating in 2026 with a regularly updated digital events calendar and Discord community.

### Part 2: Regional Comparison Across Los Angeles

* **The Valley (San Fernando Valley / Burbank / Sherman Oaks):**
  * *Verdict:* **The strongest, most self-contained board game hub in Greater LA.**
  * *Strengths:* Home to **Geeky Teas & Games** (the area's gold-standard board game lounge and cat rescue), **Guildhall** (a dedicated tabletop/esports gastropub), and **Paper Hero's Games** in Sherman Oaks, which hosts both **Friday Night Board Gaming** (weekly mid/heavy Euros) and **East Valley Board Games** (biweekly Sunday games). Easy parking, high table capacity, and weekly consistency make the Valley the easiest place in LA to build a reliable gaming routine.
* **Westside (Santa Monica / Venice / West LA):**
  * *Verdict:* **Great for casual social gamers and weekend afternoon sessions.**
  * *Strengths:* **Board Game and Brew Meetup** at Santa Monica Brew Works is one of LA’s largest and most consistent weekend groups (weekly Saturdays/Sundays), perfect for gateway games (Catan, Ticket to Ride) and social deduction. The **LAPL Venice Library** provides free monthly weekend gaming, and groups like **Westside Tabletop Adventure Games** serve indie enthusiasts.
  * *Trade-off:* Weeknight attendance can be impacted by Westside traffic, and commercial retail space limits the number of brick-and-mortar hobby stores compared to the Valley.
* **San Gabriel Valley (Pasadena / Alhambra / Arcadia):**
  * *Verdict:* **The premier destination for serious Euro strategy marathons.**
  * *Strengths:* Anchored by **Odyssey Games** in Pasadena (a massive 9,000 sq. ft. store and event space) and **LA Game Crew**. Their quarterly "Grotto" events specifically carve out 5-hour blocks for 3+ hour heavy strategy games before transitioning to evening party/gateway games.
  * *Trade-off:* Fewer casual weeknight drop-in meetups than the Valley, but unrivaled for organized weekend deep-dives.
* **Central LA / Downtown / Hollywood / Koreatown:**
  * *Verdict:* **The best area for social mixers, evening nightlife, and creative community vibes.**
  * *Strengths:* **Game Cult LA** in DTLA is an active Tuesday night scene in an immersive studio setting, blending craft beers with 100+ modern games. **Studious Game Night** in Chinatown offers a low-key, artsy community feel. **Next-Gen Games** on Pico Blvd provides a dependable central brick-and-mortar shop.
  * *Trade-off:* Street parking can be competitive; events often carry a venue entry fee ($10–$18) to offset central commercial rents.
* **South Bay & Harbor Area (Torrance / Redondo / Long Beach):**
  * *Verdict:* **Strong neighborhood bar community with steady weeknight loyalty.**
  * *Strengths:* **Long Beach Board Gamers** at The Wicked Wolf offers a weekly Wednesday night session in a private upstairs room with an active Discord and great attendance. Retail stores like **The Game Chest** at Del Amo Fashion Center (Torrance) provide gaming supplies and casual events.
  * *Trade-off:* Geographically spread out; requires driving along the 405/110 corridor if you live further north.
* **Eastside (Highland Park / Silver Lake / Echo Park / Glendale border):**
  * *Verdict:* **Pockets of community and brewery events, leaning into neighboring Pasadena and DTLA.**
  * *Strengths:* Residents have direct access to Chinatown (Studious Game Night), Burbank/Glendale (Guildhall, Geeky Teas), and Pasadena (Odyssey Games). Local breweries frequently host pop-up game nights.

### Part 3: The 6 Best Choices to Meet People and Play Regularly

These 6 distinct scenes were selected so you are not tied to a single format, crowd, or part of town:

1. **Board Game and Brew Meetup @ Santa Monica Brew Works (Westside)**
   * *Why it made the cut:* Unbeatable weekend social energy. With over 1,600 members and weekly daytime meetups, it is ideal for newcomers who want to grab a beer, sit down at a shared table, and jump into Catan or Secret Hitler without any intimidation.
2. **Geeky Teas & Games (Burbank / The Valley)**
   * *Why it made the cut:* The quintessential third-space community hub. A $5 all-day pass gives you access to a massive library, friendly regulars, knowledgeable staff, hot tea, and on-site rescue cats. It is open every day of the week, making it the easiest place to initiate or join impromptu games.
3. **LA Game Crew @ Odyssey Games (Pasadena / San Gabriel Valley)**
   * *Why it made the cut:* The gold standard for structured, serious hobby gaming. In a sprawling 9,000 sq. ft. venue, their events cleanly separate the day into a dedicated 5-hour heavy strategy/Euro block (afternoon) and an accessible newcomer session (evening).
4. **Game Cult LA @ Studio Cult (Downtown LA / Central LA)**
   * *Why it made the cut:* Best for modern weeknight nightlife. Meeting every Tuesday evening in an artistic studio with craft beers and seltzers, it turns tabletop gaming into a stylish, social 21+ night out with a curated library of modern hits like Wingspan, Azul, and Blood on the Clocktower.
5. **Friday Night Board Gaming @ Paper Hero's Games (Sherman Oaks / The Valley)**
   * *Why it made the cut:* Pure, welcoming game-store regular culture. While many store nights are dominated by collectible card games, this group has met consistently for years to play authentic European strategy games (Power Grid, Suburbia, Terraforming Mars) with patient regulars eager to teach.
6. **Long Beach Board Gamers @ The Wicked Wolf (Long Beach / South Bay Area)**
   * *Why it made the cut:* The friendliest weeknight neighborhood bar night. Meeting every Wednesday in a dedicated private upstairs room, participants sign in, grab name tags, and teach games across multiple tables with zero ego.

### Part 5: Practical Starter Plan & 1-Month Trial Routine

To explore different crowds without overcommitting, here is the recommended grouping and a week-by-week calendar order:

#### Category Breakdown:
* **Best 3 for Newcomers:**
  1. *Board Game and Brew Meetup (Santa Monica):* Zero barrier to entry, open seating, daylight brewery vibe.
  2. *Geeky Teas & Games (Burbank):* Low-pressure third space with game guides and all-day access.
  3. *Long Beach Board Gamers (The Wicked Wolf):* Name tags, organized sign-in sheet, and friendly hosts who actively seat solo attendees.
* **Best 2 for More Serious Hobby Gaming:**
  1. *LA Game Crew @ Odyssey Games (Pasadena):* The afternoon block is designed specifically for 3+ hour heavy Euros and strategic board games.
  2. *Friday Night Board Gaming @ Paper Hero's Games (Sherman Oaks):* Dedicated regulars who routinely play Power Grid, Terraforming Mars, and Suburbia.
* **Best 1 Low-Pressure Social Option:**
  1. *Game Cult LA (Downtown LA):* A Tuesday night creative mixer where socializing, grabbing a drink, and playing lighter party or deduction games like Wavelength or Codenames comes first.

#### Suggested 4-Week Trial Order:

* **Week 1 (Low-Stakes Weekend Entry):**
  * *Where:* **Board Game and Brew Meetup @ Santa Monica Brew Works** (Saturday or Sunday afternoon).
  * *Objective:* Show up solo, grab a pint or cold soda, and join an open table playing a familiar gateway game (Catan, Azul, or Secret Hitler). It gets your feet wet in a sunny, relaxed environment where half the crowd is also new.
* **Week 2 (The Dedicated Tabletop Third Space):**
  * *Where:* **Geeky Teas & Games** in Burbank (Saturday afternoon or Sunday).
  * *Objective:* Pay the $5 day pass, browse the shelves, and experience a pure board game cafe/club atmosphere. Introduce yourself to the staff or attend an open play session. This tests whether you prefer a dedicated gaming clubhouse over a bar.
* **Week 3 (Mid-Week Social Nightlife):**
  * *Where:* **Game Cult LA** in Downtown LA (Tuesday evening, 7:00 PM).
  * *Objective:* Test out an evening crowd after work. The music, creative studio setting, and mix of modern games (Wingspan, Blood on the Clocktower) will show you what LA’s weeknight social scene looks like.
* **Week 4 (The Deep Strategy / Euro Test):**
  * *Where:* **Friday Night Board Gaming @ Paper Hero's Games** (Sherman Oaks) OR **LA Game Crew @ Odyssey Games** (Pasadena).
  * *Objective:* Step up to heavier strategy gaming. Tell the table you want to learn a medium-to-heavy Euro game (like Terraforming Mars, Power Grid, or a heavy worker-placement title). You will quickly discover whether you want your regular group to be casual socializers or dedicated hobby strategists.

### Part 2: Regional Comparison Across Los Angeles

* **The Valley (San Fernando Valley / Burbank / Sherman Oaks):**
  * *Verdict:* **The strongest, most self-contained board game hub in Greater LA.**
  * *Strengths:* Home to **Geeky Teas & Games** (the area's gold-standard board game lounge and cat rescue), **Guildhall** (a dedicated tabletop/esports gastropub), and **Paper Hero's Games** in Sherman Oaks, which hosts both **Friday Night Board Gaming** (weekly mid/heavy Euros) and **East Valley Board Games** (biweekly Sunday games). Easy parking, high table capacity, and weekly consistency make the Valley the easiest place in LA to build a reliable gaming routine.
* **Westside (Santa Monica / Venice / West LA):**
  * *Verdict:* **Great for casual social gamers and weekend afternoon sessions.**
  * *Strengths:* **Board Game and Brew Meetup** at Santa Monica Brew Works is one of LA’s largest and most consistent weekend groups (weekly Saturdays/Sundays), perfect for gateway games (Catan, Ticket to Ride) and social deduction. The **LAPL Venice Library** provides free monthly weekend gaming, and groups like **Westside Tabletop Adventure Games** serve indie enthusiasts.
  * *Trade-off:* Weeknight attendance can be impacted by Westside traffic, and commercial retail space limits the number of brick-and-mortar hobby stores compared to the Valley.
* **San Gabriel Valley (Pasadena / Alhambra / Arcadia):**
  * *Verdict:* **The premier destination for serious Euro strategy marathons.**
  * *Strengths:* Anchored by **Odyssey Games** in Pasadena (a massive 9,000 sq. ft. store and event space) and **LA Game Crew**. Their quarterly "Grotto" events specifically carve out 5-hour blocks for 3+ hour heavy strategy games before transitioning to evening party/gateway games.
  * *Trade-off:* Fewer casual weeknight drop-in meetups than the Valley, but unrivaled for organized weekend deep-dives.
* **Central LA / Downtown / Hollywood / Koreatown:**
  * *Verdict:* **The best area for social mixers, evening nightlife, and creative community vibes.**
  * *Strengths:* **Game Cult LA** in DTLA is an active Tuesday night scene in an immersive studio setting, blending craft beers with 100+ modern games. **Studious Game Night** in Chinatown offers a low-key, artsy community feel. **Next-Gen Games** on Pico Blvd provides a dependable central brick-and-mortar shop.
  * *Trade-off:* Street parking can be competitive; events often carry a venue entry fee ($10–$18) to offset central commercial rents.
* **South Bay & Harbor Area (Torrance / Redondo / Long Beach):**
  * *Verdict:* **Strong neighborhood bar community with steady weeknight loyalty.**
  * *Strengths:* **Long Beach Board Gamers** at The Wicked Wolf offers a weekly Wednesday night session in a private upstairs room with an active Discord and great attendance. Retail stores like **The Game Chest** at Del Amo Fashion Center (Torrance) provide gaming supplies and casual events.
  * *Trade-off:* Geographically spread out; requires driving along the 405/110 corridor if you live further north.
* **Eastside (Highland Park / Silver Lake / Echo Park / Glendale border):**
  * *Verdict:* **Pockets of community and brewery events, leaning into neighboring Pasadena and DTLA.**
  * *Strengths:* Residents have direct access to Chinatown (Studious Game Night), Burbank/Glendale (Guildhall, Geeky Teas), and Pasadena (Odyssey Games). Local breweries frequently host pop-up game nights.
